$comment: What makes an employment contract an employment contract.
The MSA's identity comes from commercial architecture -- how work is ordered, priced,
governed and exited. This one's comes largely from STATUTE: the Code on Wages fixes
when and how much is paid, the POSH Act imposes a duty that does not depend on the
contract, EPF and gratuity attach on thresholds nobody negotiates. That is the point
of authoring this second registry: if the Requirement -> Treatment -> Clause model only
works where the parties freely design the bargain, it is an MSA implementation rather
Statutory entitlements are NOT requirements merely because they exist. They are
requirements where the contract's silence causes a legal defect -- which is what the
'Remove it and ...' test is for. An employee's right to gratuity does not depend on the
contract mentioning it; a contract that misstates the wage structure does cause harm.

requirements.statement: The position, its duties and the place of work are identified.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and there is no ascertainable subject matter: neither party can say what was agreed to be done or where.

falsification.attack: Assessed an employment contract without establishing the employer's headcount, the employee's sex, or whether the role creates copyright.
falsification.false_green: Three requirements including the POSH duty reported NOT_APPLICABLE — skipped rather than assessed, because an unanswered fact read as an answer of no.

requirements.statement: What the employee is paid, and the period by reference to which it is paid, is stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the contract fails for want of consideration, and section 15 of the Code on Wages, 2019 has no wage period to attach to.

requirements.statement: The split between wages and other components is stated in a way that can be tested against the statutory definition.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and a cost-to-company figure conceals whether basic wages meet the fifty per cent floor implied by section 2(y) of the Code on Wages, 2019 — which decides gratuity, provident fund and retrenchment compensation for the whole of the employment.

requirements.statement: When wages fall due is fixed.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and sections 16 and 17 of the Code on Wages, 2019 supply the answer by default, which is rarely what either party assumed.

requirements.statement: Hours of work, and the treatment of work beyond them, are stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the employer cannot show compliance with the daily and weekly limits, and overtime liability is computed against an unstated norm.

requirements.statement: Leave entitlement is stated and is not below the statutory floor.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and entitlement is whatever the applicable Shops and Establishments Act provides, which varies by state and which neither party has read.

requirements.statement: How either side ends the employment, on what notice, and what is payable on exit.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and separation is governed by implied terms and state legislation, and the employee has no stated route out at all.

requirements.statement: A procedure exists before an employee is disciplined or dismissed for cause.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and a dismissal for misconduct is open to challenge for want of natural justice, whatever the substance of the allegation.

requirements.statement: The employee has a stated route for raising a grievance.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and section 4 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 requires a grievance redressal committee that the contract does not reflect.

requirements.statement: The employer's duty to provide a workplace free of sexual harassment is reflected in the contract.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the contract is silent on a duty section 19 of the POSH Act, 2013 places on the employer, leaving an employee with no contractual notice of it.
$split: One half of POSH_DUTY_REFLECTED, which named two duties with different triggers and
gated both on headcount. Its own identity_test said section 19 imposes its duty
'regardless', and its applicability was employer_headcount_ge_10 == true, so the
requirement reported inapplicable for a workplace its own words said was covered.
VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE: that section 19's duties attach without a headcount threshold,
and which of them a contract of employment should reflect as distinct from a workplace
policy. The split follows what the requirement already asserted; the assertion itself
has not been checked against the Act by an advocate.
requirements.$verification_needed: POSH Act, 2013 s.19 — whether the listed employer duties apply irrespective of the number of workers.

requirements.statement: Where the workplace employs ten or more, the Internal Committee the Act requires is reflected.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and an employee at a workplace required to have an Internal Committee is left unaware of the forum section 4 exists to provide, and of how to reach it.
$split: The other half. The threshold belongs to this duty and not to the one above.
POSH_INTERNAL_COMMITTEE_001 states the same threshold in its own text: 'at each
workplace employing ten or more employees'.
VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE: the threshold and who counts toward it.
requirements.$verification_needed: POSH Act, 2013 s.4 — the composition of the Internal Committee and who is counted toward the ten.
requirements.$kind_open: CONTENT is satisfied by the contract describing the Internal Committee. It cannot establish that a Committee was ever constituted under s.4. If the requirement is meant to reach the body's existence, this is EXTERNAL_COHERENCE and no clause can satisfy it.

requirements.statement: Confidential information is protected, and the protection does not survive as a restraint on the employee's livelihood.
requirements.identity_test: Remove the bound and section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 may void the protection entirely as against a departing employee.

requirements.statement: Who owns what the employee creates is stated.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and section 17(c) of the Copyright Act, 1957 vests first ownership in the employer only for work made under a contract of service in the course of employment — which leaves everything at the edges disputed.
$repaired: Was gated on assigns_copyright == true, which is directionally backwards. The
identity_test's whole argument is about the gap section 17(c) leaves — work at the
edges of 'in the course of employment' — and that gap is WIDEST where nothing has been
assigned. Gating on assignment being present meant the requirement applied only where
the gap was already smallest.
Unconditional now, which is what the statement says: 'Who owns what the employee
creates is stated.' Every contract of service states it or leaves it to section 17(c)
and to argument. The three-state intake field ip_ownership ('Employer owns work product
IP' / 'Employee retains pre-existing IP only' / 'Custom / shared arrangement') is what
SATISFIES it; assigns_copyright was a boolean flattening of that field being used to
decide whether the question arose at all.
VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE: whether any contract of service should be treated as not
needing this — an engagement creating no copyrightable work product, for instance.

requirements.statement: Maternity benefit entitlement is reflected where the establishment is covered.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the contract is silent on an entitlement the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 confers by section 5 and which the employer may not lawfully reduce.
$repaired: Was gated on is_female_employee == true while the statement said 'where the
establishment is covered'. Two different boundaries, and the requirement named the one
it did not implement.
Now gated on establishment coverage, which is what the statement says. The employee's
sex is not the condition: a contract at a covered establishment should reflect the
entitlement whoever currently holds the post, and gating a contractual term on an
employee's sex is a drafting question in its own right.
VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE: the Maternity Benefit Act's coverage threshold, and whether
eligibility of the individual employee (service qualification under section 5) belongs
here as a second condition or is a matter for the clause's own wording.
requirements.$kind_open: Same shape. The contract reflecting the entitlement is CONTENT; whether the establishment is in fact covered is a record elsewhere.

requirements.statement: Provident fund, insurance and retirement benefits are addressed.
requirements.identity_test: Remove it and the employee cannot tell from the contract whether the employer treats the establishment as covered by the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, which decides what is deducted from the wages stated in it.
requirements.$kind_open: The contract addressing PF, ESI and retirement benefits is CONTENT. Actual registration under the 1952 Act is a FORMALITY performed outside the instrument, and this requirement does not reach it.

$kind_basis: WHY EVERY REQUIREMENT HERE IS `kind: CONTENT`.
documentRequirements.admit began refusing records with no `kind`, and these two files were never
updated — so every document type failed to generate, because the loader admits all requirement
sources globally before any clause is assembled.
CONTENT is not a guess and not a convenience. It is what the loader was already applying
silently, and each record's own identity_test confirms it: every one of them turns on what a
reader can or cannot tell FROM THE CONTRACT. SOCIAL_SECURITY_ADDRESSED says it outright — remove
it and 'the employee cannot tell from the contract'. MATERNITY_ENTITLEMENT — 'the contract is
silent on an entitlement'. So declaring CONTENT records the existing behaviour rather than
changing it, and the guard's complaint was the silence, not the value.
FOUR ARE WORTH AN ADVOCATE'S EYE, and are marked `$kind_open` rather than left to look settled.
In each, the document reflecting a thing and the thing existing are not the same, and CONTENT
